Plan the round: click the stations in order

Part 1 · summary

What part 1 settled

  • A round looks, listens and reads what no screen shows.
  • The pilot has 24 local instruments of four kinds.
  • Most have a DCS partner, so a round checks the screens.
  • A planned order covers grade, both platforms and the gas shelter.

Part 2 · How the instruments work

How does each kind of local instrument work, and how is it read?

Part 2 · the plan

Four instruments, four ways to read

  1. Bourdon gaugea curved tube that straightens with pressure; choosing the range
  2. Bimetal thermometera coil that turns with temperature, and why to wait
  3. Sight glasslevel in the glass equals level in the vessel
  4. Flow glass and displaysyes/no flow; numbers read as shown
  5. Reading a dialto half a division, square to the face

Part 2 · Bourdon gauge

A curved tube that straightens with pressure

Tube movement exaggerated. Gauge 0–60 bar g, as PG-602.

Pressure inside the flattened tube uncurls it; a linkage turns the pointer. Above full scale the pointer sits on the stop.

Part 2 · Bourdon gauge

Is each gauge in the middle of its scale?

Good practice (typical, assumed): normal reading in the middle half, 25–75 % of span.

Readings from

A gauge near zero reads coarsely; one near full scale has no margin for a pressure rise.

Part 2 · bimetal thermometer

Wait for the thermometer

$$T_d=T_0+\Delta T\,(1-e^{-t/\tau})$$

Two strips that expand differently make a coil turn. In a thermowell it lags: read after the needle stops. τ values assumed.

Part 2 · sight glass

Level glass: same level, different volume

The glass shows height. In a horizontal drum, half height is half volume, but 20 % height is far less than 20 % volume.

Part 2 · sight glass

From glass height to litres

$$\frac{V}{V_{full}}=\frac{\theta-\sin\theta}{2\pi},\qquad \theta=2\arccos\left(1-\frac{2h}{D}\right)$$
$h$
liquid height read on the glass
m
$D$
drum inside diameter (EQL rev A1)
m
$\theta$
angle the liquid surface subtends at the axis
rad

Heads are ignored, and the glass is assumed to span the full diameter.

Part 2 · flow glass and displays

Yes/no instruments and digital displays

Flow glass FG-602

Shows gas moving, not how much: flowing above about 1 NL/min (Field tab rule).

Displays

Read as shown, with the unit printed on them.

Heater controller displays.

Gas flow-control station.

Part 2 · reading a dial

Read the dial, then compare

Your reading

Read square to the face, to half a minor division; a reading closer than that is not real.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • A Bourdon tube uncurls with pressure; read it in the middle half of its scale.
  • A bimetal dial lags: wait until the needle stops.
  • A glass shows height; volume in a horizontal drum needs geometry.
  • Read a dial to half a minor division.

Part 3 · the round sheet

The round sheet: read first, then the DCS

The sheet carries no expected values: write what the needle shows, with time and unit, before looking at the screen.

Part 3 · tolerance

How far may field and DCS differ?

$$|x_F-x_D|\le a_F S_F+a_D S_D+r$$
$x_F,\ x_D$
field reading · DCS value
units
$a_F,\ a_D$
accuracy: gauge class, e.g. 1 % · transmitter, e.g. 0.1 % (assumed)
% span
$S_F,\ S_D$
spans of the gauge and of the transmitter
units
$r$
reading resolution, half a minor division
units

Part 3 · tolerance

Tolerance calculator

A coarse gauge on a wide span gives a wide band: inside it, a difference is not evidence of anything.

Part 3 · explained differences

Four honest reasons to disagree

Location

Gauge and transmitter on different points of a line.

Height

Liquid-filled leg: 1 m of ethanol adds 0.077 bar.

Units

bar g vs bar a; NL/min vs L/min.

Time

Moving values read minutes apart.

Explain a difference before calling an instrument wrong: Δp = ρ g h, with ρ = 789 kg/m³ for ethanol.

Part 3 · discrepancy finder

Agree, explained, or write it up?

Put tolerance and the four reasons to work on real pairs.

Seven neutral cases from the design state: tolerance first, then a reason, then a report.

Part 3 · checks of this unit

Typical field checks, station by station

Normal values come from the simulator's design state; a round records them, it does not adjust them.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • Write the reading, time and unit before looking at the DCS.
  • Tolerance adds both accuracies and the reading resolution.
  • Location, height, units and time explain many differences.
  • Report only what tolerance and reasons cannot explain.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Plan the round so every local instrument is visited once, in a short order.

2

Read square to the face, to half a division, after the needle settles.

3

Compare with the DCS only after writing your own reading.

4

Judge a difference against tolerance and known reasons before reporting it.
